definition: Uncertain inference was first described by C.
details: J. van Rijsbergen as a way to formally define a query and document relationship in Information retrieval. This formalization is a logical implication with an attached measure of uncertainty.

explainer.lead: Uncertain inference formalizes a query and document relationship as a logical implication carrying a measure of uncertainty. It matters in information retrieval for reasoning when relationships are not certain.

tiers.eli5: Instead of saying 'this document definitely matches', it says 'this document probably matches, with this much confidence'.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to define query-document relationships in information retrieval with attached uncertainty. A pitfall is that the result depends on the chosen measure of uncertainty.
tiers.paperLevel: First described by C. J. van Rijsbergen, uncertain inference is a logical implication with an attached measure of uncertainty, used to formally define a query and document relationship in information retrieval.

explainer.example: A search system scores a document against a query as a logical implication with an attached uncertainty measure rather than a binary match.
